overview: The Emperor’s Children pursue perfection, while the friendship between Fulgrim and Ferrus Manus faces the gathering crisis.
synopsis: Fulgrim’s Emperor’s Children seek to make every act of war and art an expression of perfection. The campaign against the Laer brings the Legion into contact with a weapon and a culture whose influence reaches far beyond the battlefield. Artists aboard the fleet mirror the warriors’ growing obsession.

The bond between Fulgrim and Ferrus Manus is tested as the civil war gathers pace. Officers including Lucius and Saul Tarvitz take different paths through the Legion’s changing culture, while the campaigns at Isstvan turn private corruption into irreversible public violence.
detailed: The Emperor’s Children attack the Laer, determined to complete a difficult conquest quickly and demonstrate their superiority. Fulgrim takes a blade from a Laer temple. Its influence enters his private thoughts while the Legion’s pursuit of perfection becomes increasingly detached from restraint.

The remembrancers and artists travelling with the Legion undergo their own transformations. Ostian Delafour and Serena d’Angelus represent very different responses to the desire to create something transcendent. The activities of Fabius and the Legion’s altered attitudes to sensation show corruption spreading through multiple parts of the expedition.

Fulgrim’s relationship with Ferrus Manus provides a contrast to these developments. Their friendship is expressed through gifts, competition and shared history. When Fulgrim attempts to bring Ferrus to Horus’s cause, the encounter exposes a division that affection cannot overcome.

The betrayal at Isstvan III and the subsequent gathering at Isstvan V bring the Legions into open civil war. Ferrus leads the Iron Hands into the fighting with a personal determination to confront Fulgrim. The arrival of the second wave transforms the battle into a trap for the loyalist forces.

Fulgrim kills Ferrus during their confrontation. The immediate horror of the act breaks through his self-justification, but the presence associated with the blade takes control. Fulgrim is left trapped within his own consciousness as the Legion continues down its new path.
